clue.text: Bear to carry round the French artist

indicators.note: to carry something round another is to wrap it about the outside, so one word encloses the rest

blocks.note: to tote is to carry
le is French for the
RA, Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to put up with lugging a French painter around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal or a burden to carry, but it is the verb meaning endure; carrying is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it or endure it without complaint.

clue.text: Also includes half-mature fruit

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters are kept
includes means the first word holds the next inside it

blocks.note: too means also
taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: A bowl that also contains fruit that is only half ripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the seed-bearing berry of the plant.

clue.text: Myth to support death

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or a body
death is the end

explanation.surface: A tale that holds up even past the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, popularly believed but unverified, much like a myth.

clue.text: Diamonds with paste in the middle are hard but edible at tea time, say

definitions.text: hard but edible at tea time, say

indicators.note: something in the middle sits inside the other word, splitting it

blocks.note: rocks is slang for diamonds
to cake is to coat thickly, as with a paste

explanation.surface: Jewels with fake paste set in the centre are tough but somehow eaten at afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Paste is also fake jewellery, steering the solver toward gems. Rock cakes are small British buns with a rough, hard surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock cakes are small currant buns with a craggy crust, typically served with afternoon tea.

clue.text: New Australian navy giving up gold to reach the land of Dracula

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters are rearranged
giving something up means surrendering it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A rebuilt Australian fleet sacrifices its gold to sail to Dracula's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker set Count Dracula's castle in Transylvania, a region of Romania.

clue.text: Gunman takes bearing, pulls back pin and turns about

indicators.note: pulling a word back drags its letters into the opposite order
a word that turns faces the other way, so it is read right to left

blocks.note: south, a compass bearing
taken as written, then read backwards
re means about or concerning, then read backwards

explanation.surface: A gunman takes aim, draws back the firing pin and swings round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a gunman who shoots from a hidden position, often at long range.

clue.text: I'm returning to love a new girl

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is coming back to romance with a different girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name, as from the Book of Ruth; crosswords use girl for any female name.

clue.text: Use traps around the meadows

indicators.note: around suggests moving things about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper is told to lay snares across the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastures are grassland fields used for grazing, the same kind of land as meadows.

clue.text: Callous girl gets reduced amount

blocks.note: Ruth is a girl's name
less is a smaller amount

explanation.surface: An unfeeling young woman gets a smaller share.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means without pity or compassion, heartless just like callous.

clue.text: Enchanting Scotsman is a conjuror

blocks.note: magic as an adjective means enchanting
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A charming Scot turns out to be a stage magician.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror performs tricks and illusions for an audience, the work of a stage magic act.

clue.text: Mollycoddle company of saints by knocking back endless tea

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the last letter goes
knocking back a drink tips it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
SS is the abbreviation for saints
taken as written, then trimmed and turned

explanation.surface: A fussy group of saints spoils itself by gulping down tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or overprotect, exactly what mollycoddling someone means.

clue.text: Harsh regime uses mounted police to give thanks to kingship

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounted means climbing upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British detective police branch
ta is British informal for thanks
taken as written
read as king plus ship: R for rex, Latin for king, then ship as written

explanation.surface: An oppressive government deploys mounted police to make people bow to the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingship is split into king and ship; mounted police suggests horses but means the letters go upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictatorship is government by one absolute ruler, typically oppressive, so a harsh regime.

clue.text: Soft drink to make you feel better

definitions.note: a phrase for something that makes you feel better; the answer is a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the fizzy mixer
second meaning: a restorative medicine or pick-me-up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a drink that perks you up; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a carbonated mixer, and a tonic is also a restorative medicine or anything invigorating.

clue.text: "It's Paul, right" I managed. "Divine!"

indicators.note: something managed has been handled and arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recognising Paul manages to compliment him: divine!
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual and divine both describe things of God or the soul rather than the material world.

clue.text: Thousands backing the Spanish and French on Florida islands; they will open any door

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the letters for thousands are read backwards

blocks.note: K stands for a thousand, so thousands are Ks
el is Spanish for the
with and, et is French for and
taken as written
the Florida Keys are a chain of islands

explanation.surface: Thousands of Spanish and French holidaymakers flock to the Florida islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and French' together give ET, French for and; 'and' is not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key is a master key with its wards filed away, so it fits many different locks.

clue.text: I-Informer in simple surrounding tells a story

indicators.note: in places the stammered informer inside the word that follows
surrounding says the word for simple wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: naive means simple or unsophisticated
an informer is a rat; the clue's stammer is copied, so it comes out as R-RAT

explanation.surface: A nervous informant stammers out a tale to a gullible listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in I-Informer is the trick: the word for an informer gets the same stammer, its first letter doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: Mysterious Eastern drunkard cooked rice

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters of the grain are reworked

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
a sot is a habitual drunkard
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An enigmatic oriental drunk makes himself some rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric describes knowledge understood only by a few initiates, hence obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Attendants throw casserole half skywards

indicators.note: half means only one of the two halves of the following word is kept

blocks.note: a stew is a casserole
taken as written; its back half is kept

explanation.surface: Waiters fling a casserole halfway up to the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are attendants who look after passengers on ships, planes and trains.

clue.text: Is a story fact muddled? That's acceptable

indicators.note: something muddled is jumbled up, so the letters before it are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs about a confused account: if the facts are muddled, that will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means good enough to meet requirements, the same as acceptable.

clue.text: Expedition to see South Africa playing fair

indicators.note: playing with something moves it around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Tourists travel to watch the South African team play by the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to observe or hunt wild animals, especially in Africa.

clue.text: Interfere to get a military decoration, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is something spoken, matching a phrase by its sound

blocks.note: a medal is a military decoration

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone pulled strings to win a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere in matters that are not one's concern.

clue.text: Old news broadcaster may weep for the community

blocks.note: a town is a community
one who may weep is a crier

explanation.surface: An old-time newsreader might shed tears on behalf of his neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'crier for the town', so the second piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers, a town crier rang a bell and shouted public announcements in the streets.

clue.text: React wildly to provide food

indicators.note: wildly means in an uncontrolled way, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone overreacts when asked to make the meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply meals and refreshments, as for a party or event.

clue.text: Stone found in the crag at Edale

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A rock hunter picks up a gemstone on a crag near Edale.
explanation.walkthrough: Edale is a village in the Peak District of England, popular with walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Rite almost enveloped in beam of sunlight - that's something unusual

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something enveloped in another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: a ray is a beam of light
taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A ceremony bathed in a shaft of sunlight is a remarkable sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is a thing seldom found or seen, hence something out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Thunder drops below, so it's excellent to come down somewhere in South-East Asia

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a word for below is removed

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut
under means below; this is the part removed
A1 means excellent, written with the letter I for the one
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: A storm rumbles beneath an aircraft, so it is a relief to touch down in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a kingdom in South-East Asia, between Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia.

clue.text: Cuban leader orders actors about

indicators.note: to order the cast around is to arrange them, putting the letters into a new order
about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictator bosses a group of performers around.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba after the 1959 revolution, as prime minister and then president.

clue.text: By the sound of it, cheery and drunk Cockney has a craving for food

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words
says the pieces are to be judged by how they are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: happy, with the H dropped in Cockney speech
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A merry, tipsy Londoner fancies something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the natural desire to eat, a hunger or craving for food.
